headline: WhatsApp lets users reserve usernames before launch later this year
summary: Users can now reserve a unique handle for WhatsApp, which is set to launch later this year. The feature allows users to choose a username that will be used to identify them on the platform.
details: WhatsApp has started allowing users to reserve usernames before the feature officially launches later this year. This move is aimed at allowing users to secure their desired usernames before they are taken.
The username reservation feature is available now for users who are running the latest version of WhatsApp. To reserve a username, users need to go to Settings > Account > Username.

It's worth noting that users will still need a valid phone number when registering for WhatsApp for the first time. However, after that, they can choose to share their phone number or username with new contacts.
The introduction of usernames is a significant move for WhatsApp, which has over 3 billion users. The platform is trying to give users more control over their identity on the app.

topic: Designing reliable queueing and message-broker layers in PMS platforms
headline_marked: [[Queueing & Message-Broker Layers]] enable reliable PMS platforms
headline: Queueing & Message-Broker Layers enable reliable PMS platforms
summary: Free PMS platforms rely on robust queueing and message-broker layers for seamless operations.
details: Modern Property Management Systems depend on continuous data exchange between internal modules and external services. Bookings, calendar updates, guest communication, cleaning tasks, and maintenance triggers all generate operational events that must be processed quickly and reliably.
Free PMS platforms such as PMS.Rent rely on robust queueing and message-broker layers to ensure that these events never get lost and are always processed in the correct order.
The architecture enables the PMS to scale horizontally, maintain predictable performance, and avoid bottlenecks during peak operational periods.
caption:
Can PMS platforms handle thousands of daily operations without delays?

Modern Property Management Systems depend on continuous data exchange between internal modules and external services. Bookings, calendar updates, guest communication, cleaning tasks, and maintenance triggers all generate operational events that must be processed quickly and reliably.

Free PMS platforms such as PMS.Rent rely on robust queueing and message-broker layers to ensure that these events never get lost and are always processed in the correct order.

The architecture enables the PMS to scale horizontally, maintain predictable performance, and avoid bottlenecks during peak operational periods.
